Work in /Users/jaxson/Downloads/codingprojects/support-agent-demo (Python 3.13, uv). TOP PRIORITY task: make each eval case produce ONE neatlogs trace with child spans, instead of the current state where each model call lands as a separate trace with 0 spans (so span-level divergence in AgentBisect never works).

Do:
1. Read agent/tracing.py, agent/loop.py, evals/harness.py, and the installed neatlogs SDK (find it under .venv site-packages; check its docs/README/reference for the trace-context / span API — e.g. neatlogs.span, trace context managers, OTel parent context). Make sure neatlogs instrumentation is actually on (init before client creation, wrap client, flush+shutdown at end of process).
2. Wrap each case run in one parent span/trace (named e.g. `support_case`, with case id tag), and each tool call as a child span (name `tool:<tool_name>`, with args and result/error as attributes) and each model call as a child. Use the real public trace-context API from the SDK reference; avoid private internals if a public API works.
3. Validate live: .env in the repo has NEATLOGS_API_KEY and project id. Run one case (agent uses AGENT_MODEL=claude-haiku-5-5 via the claude -p proxy the agentbisect repo provides: `cd ../agentbisect && uv run agentbisect llm-proxy --help` — read agentbisect/llm_proxy.py for how to start it and how the demo points at it via ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL). Then read the trace back with `~/.local/neatlogs-cli/bin/neatlogs` (profile neatlogs-us; see `--help`) and confirm: one trace id, N>0 spans, tool spans are children. Report the trace id and span count.
4. Also add a deliberately flaky tool: one mocked tool (pick lookup of shipping/tracking or search_help) raises a timeout ~30% of the time, deterministic per (case, repeat) seed via env var DEMO_FLAKE_SEED so it is reproducible, off when DEMO_FLAKE=0. Agent should handle the timeout via a retry or graceful message (as a natural recovery path). Don't change planted-regression behavior at any historical commit; this is new HEAD-only work, and keep ground truth/regression commits untouched (new commits on top).
5. Tests must pass (uv run pytest). One commit for tracing, a separate commit for the flaky tool. Commit messages end with: Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>. Push to origin main when done. Do not touch the agentbisect repo. Do not hard-code any key in committed files.
Report: commit shas, trace id + span count verified, anything unverified.

- animate: Build an animation from scratch, making the decisions in the order that determines whether it feels right — should it animate at all, what purpose, which tool, which properties, which curve and duration, how it interrupts, how it exits. Writes the implementation. Use when asked to animate something, add motion, make a component feel alive, or build a transition. For critiquing existing motion use review-animations; for auditing a whole codebase use improve-animations.
- animation-vocabulary: Reverse-lookup glossary that turns a vague description of a web animation or motion effect into its exact term ("the bouncy thing when a popover opens" → Pop in; "the iOS rubber-band scroll" → Rubber-banding). Use when the user asks "what's it called when…", or describes a motion effect without knowing its name and wants the right word to prompt an AI or designer with. For naming an effect, not designing or building one.
- apple-design: Apple's approach to interface design and fluid, physical motion, translated for the web. Use when building or reviewing gesture-driven UI, spring animations, drag/swipe/sheet interactions, momentum and interruptible transitions, translucent materials and depth, typography (optical sizing, tracking, leading), reduced-motion, or the design foundations (feedback, spatial consistency, restraint) behind Apple-style interfaces.
- application-form-filler: Fill out job application form fields with context-aware, tailored answers drawn from the candidate's CV and the job description
- baseline-ui: Quickly deslop UI code by fixing spacing, hierarchy, typography, and small layout issues. Use when the interface needs a fast cleanup or polish pass.
- better-accessibility: Accessibility engineering for product interfaces, from focus states and keyboard support to ARIA, forms, and screen readers. Use when building or reviewing UI components, modals, menus, forms, custom widgets, or when the user says "make this accessible" or reports keyboard or screen-reader issues. Triggers on accessibility, a11y, WCAG, aria, focus ring, focus-visible, focus trap, keyboard navigation, tab order, tabindex, screen reader, sr-only, aria-live, alt text, hit area, touch target, prefers-reduced-motion, autoplay, toast duration, skip link, semantic HTML, aria-label, form errors, disabled buttons, "not keyboard accessible".

Triggers on UX writing, microcopy, interface copy, product copy, copywriting, button labels, link text, error messages, empty states, placeholder text, settings labels, capitalization, title case, sentence case, voice and tone.

- brutalist-skill (industrial-brutalist-ui): Raw mechanical interfaces fusing Swiss typographic print with military terminal aesthetics. Rigid grids, extreme type scale contrast, utilitarian color, analog degradation effects. For data-heavy dashboards, portfolios, or editorial sites that need to feel like declassified blueprints.

- cold-email-writer: Write personalized cold outreach emails to hiring managers and founders — specific, human, not a pitch deck

- fixing-metadata: Audit and fix HTML metadata including page titles, meta descriptions, canonical URLs, Open Graph tags, Twitter cards, favicons, JSON-LD structured data, and robots directives. - fixing-motion-performance: Audit and fix animation performance issues including layout thrashing, compositor properties, scroll-linked motion, and blur effects. Use when animations stutter, transitions jank, or reviewing CSS/JS animation performance.

Enforces Python-driven true randomization for layout variance, strict AIDA page structure, wide editorial typography (bans 6-line wraps), gapless bento grids, strict GSAP ScrollTriggers (pinning, stacking, scrubbing), inline micro-images, and massive section spacing.

HyperFrames is the default output framework unless the user explicitly chooses another framework for the deliverable or asks only to record a browser session.

Also covers Tailwind projects and the STORYBOARD.md / SCRIPT.md plan formats. Read before writing composition HTML.

- imagegen-frontend-mobile: Elite mobile app image-generation skill for creating premium, app-native screen concepts and flows. Designed for iOS, Android, and cross-platform mobile products. Prioritizes clean hierarchy, comfortably readable text, strong multi-screen consistency, controlled color palettes, non-generic creative direction, textured surfaces, image-led composition, tasteful custom iconography, and clean phone mockup framing. By default, screens should be shown inside a subtle premium iPhone or similar phone mockup with a visible frame, while the main focus stays on the app content itself. This skill generates images only. It does not write code.
- imagegen-frontend-web: Elite frontend image-direction skill for generating premium, conversion-aware website design references. CRITICAL OUTPUT RULE — generate ONE separate horizontal image FOR EVERY section. A landing page with 8 sections produces 8 images. Never compress multiple sections into one image. Enforces composition variety (not always left-text / right-image), background-image freedom, varied CTAs, varied hero scales (giant / mid / mini minimalist), narrative concept spine, second-read moments, and a single consistent palette across all images. Optimized for landing pages, marketing sites, and product comps that developers or coding models can accurately recreate.
- improve-animations: Survey a codebase's animation and motion code as a senior motion advisor, then produce a prioritized audit and self-contained implementation plans for other agents (or cheaper models) to execute. Read-only on source code — it plans improvements, it does not apply them. Use when the user asks to "improve the animations", "audit the motion", "make this app feel better", or wants a roadmap of animation fixes rather than a review of a single diff.
- improve-ui: Audit an existing product surface against its own design evidence, identify verified UI problems, and write self-contained implementation plans for another agent. Strictly read-only on product source. Use when asked to review, refine, improve, or clean up an interface without replacing its identity; investigate design-system drift; or prepare a design handoff.
- interface-review: User-invoked interface review of a change rather than a screen: uncommitted work, the current branch, or a pull request. Resolves the change scope, expands it to the surfaces it affects, reads both sides of the diff, and classifies every finding as introduced, a regression, or pre-existing, then hands the review to better-interface for domain routing, severity, and the verdict. Covers interface quality, not correctness, tests, or security. Supports quick and full review modes. Triggers on interface-review, review my branch, review my PR, review the diff, review my changes, review before pushing, design regression check, changed files interface review.

- job-description-analyzer: Analyze job postings, calculate match scores, identify gaps, and create application strategy
- linkedin-profile-optimizer: Optimize LinkedIn profile for searchability, recruiter visibility, and engagement
- media-use: Agent Media OS, the single skill for every media need in a HyperFrames project. Keeps search noise on disk, hands the agent one path or block. Use for any audio, image, icon, logo, voiceover, caption, color-grading, or media-asset need.

- offer-comparison-analyzer: Compare multiple job offers side-by-side with total compensation analysis
- output-skill (full-output-enforcement): Overrides default LLM truncation behavior. Enforces complete code generation, bans placeholder patterns, and handles token-limit splits cleanly. Apply to any task requiring exhaustive, unabridged output.
- portfolio-case-study-writer: Transform resume bullets into detailed portfolio case studies
- redesign-skill (redesign-existing-projects): Upgrades existing websites and apps to premium quality. Audits current design, identifies generic AI patterns, and applies high-end design standards without breaking functionality. Works with any CSS framework or vanilla CSS.
- reference-list-builder: Format professional references properly and prepare reference materials
- resume-ats-optimizer: Optimize resumes for Applicant Tracking Systems, check ATS compatibility, and analyze keyword match
- resume-bullet-writer: Transform weak resume bullets into achievement-focused statements with metrics and impact
- resume-formatter: Ensure ATS-friendly formatting and create clean scannable layouts
- resume-quantifier: Find opportunities to add metrics and estimate numbers when exact data unavailable
- resume-section-builder: Create targeted resume sections optimized for different experience levels and roles
- resume-tailor: Customize resume for specific job postings while maintaining truthfulness
- resume-version-manager: Track different resume versions, maintain master resume, manage tailored versions
- salary-negotiation-prep: Research market rates, build negotiation strategy, and create counter-offer scripts
- slide-studio: Create, edit, visually inspect, and export Slide Studio carousel slides through the local Slide Studio MCP companion.
- soft-skill (high-end-visual-design): Teaches the AI to design like a high-end agency. Defines the exact fonts, spacing, shadows, card structures, and animations that make a website feel expensive. Blocks all the common defaults that make AI designs look cheap or generic.
- stitch-skill (stitch-design-taste): Semantic Design System Skill for Google Stitch. Generates agent-friendly DESIGN.md files that enforce premium, anti-generic UI standards — strict typography, calibrated color, asymmetric layouts, perpetual micro-motion, and hardware-accelerated performance.
- taste-skill (design-taste-frontend): Anti-slop frontend skill for landing pages, portfolios, and redesigns. - tech-resume-optimizer: Optimize resumes for software engineering, PM, and technical roles
- ui-skills-root: Use before UI-related work to select the smallest useful UI Skills context through the ui-skills CLI.
- composio:composio-connect: Connect an app/toolkit to Composio via managed OAuth (e.g. Slack, GitHub, Gmail).
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- plugin-authoring: Make a mod: a change to Claude's own interface or behaviour, such as a live pane or panel, a band above the prompt, a status line, a toast, a slash command, or a hook on tool calls or prompts. Use to make, change or debug a mod or its hooks module.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.

# Large multi-feature tasks

When a request is big — multiple features, or a large ask that naturally splits into independent
pieces of work — do not implement it as one monolithic pass. Split it into separate commits, one
per feature/unit of work, and drive each unit through this graph-engineering framework using the
Agent tool:

```
Task -> Planner -> Worker -> [Reviewer 1, Reviewer 2, ... Reviewer N] -> Synthesise -> Pass?
                     ^                                                        |
                     |-------------------- feedback (no) ---------------------|
                                                                               |
                                                                          (yes) -> commit -> next unit
```

- **Planner**: breaks the overall ask into an ordered list of commit-sized units of work (a
  Plan Reviewer can review the plan itself before execution starts; route its feedback back to
  the Planner and send a summary of plan feedback to the user).
- **Worker**: a resident agent (kept alive across the reviewer round for a given unit) that
  implements one unit of work.
- **Reviewers (1..N)**: spawn multiple reviewer agents in parallel against the Worker's output —
  e.g. correctness, simplification/efficiency, and test coverage as separate reviewer passes.
  These can be ephemeral (fresh agent per round).
- **Synthesise**: reconcile the reviewers' findings into one set of required changes.
- **Pass? gate**: if synthesised feedback has no blocking issues, finalize and commit that unit
  with its own commit message, then move to the next planned unit. If it fails, send the
  synthesised feedback back to the Worker as another round on the same unit (don't restart from
  the Planner unless the feedback reveals the plan itself was wrong).

Net effect: one commit per feature/unit, each vetted by multiple reviewer passes before it lands,
rather than a single large uncommitted or unreviewed diff at the end.

## Verifying UI work: visual recreation (the main way to verify)

For any unit that changes UI, the primary verification is a **visual recreation**: render the real
components with mock data and look at a screenshot. Typecheck and unit tests are necessary but do not
count as verifying how it looks. Workers should do this before reporting, and I re-do it (or open the
image for the user) when the user asks to see it.

1. Add a **temporary** preview route (e.g. `apps/web/app/zz-preview/page.tsx`) that imports the real
   components and renders them with realistic mock props: populated, empty, capped/failed, long
   names/links. Put context around them (page background, a mock frame for panels/drawers that need a
   session or client state) but never reimplement the component itself.
2. Start the dev server in the background with dummy env vars the app needs to boot (e.g.
   `CONVEX_URL=https://dummy.convex.cloud CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY=x NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 bunx next dev -p <port>`),
   wait for "Ready", and `curl` the route for a 200.
3. Screenshot with headless Chrome, not the preview MCP tools (those time out):
   `"/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" --headless=new --disable-gpu --hide-scrollbars --force-device-scale-factor=2 --virtual-time-budget=6000 --window-size=<w>,<h> --screenshot=/tmp/<name>.png <url>`
   Take a wide desktop shot and a narrow one. Headless Chrome enforces a minimum window width, so a
   narrow shot can come out horizontally clipped; for true 320px checks render inside a 320px-wide
   iframe or measure element widths, and say so rather than treating clipping as a bug.
4. **Read the PNG** (the Read tool shows images) and actually look at it: hierarchy, spacing, truncation,
   overflow, alignment, tap targets, copy. Report what was seen versus what was not verified
   (hover/focus states, real clipboard/share, animations, Safari-only behavior, the real page behind auth).
5. For the user, `open` the desktop screenshot (copy it to `~/Downloads/<name>.png` first) since they
   can't see tool-output images.
6. **Clean up before committing**: stop the dev server (`pkill -f "next dev -p <port>"`), delete the
   preview route, temp public files and stray `.next` artifacts, and confirm `git status` shows only
   intended changes. Never commit a preview route or mocks.

# Mandatory visual + local-server verification (every agent, every run)

Applies to any task that changes code a user can see or that the running app depends on. No unit of
work is "done" until both of these have happened and been reported:

1. **Run it against the local server.** Start the real dev server (and `npx convex dev` when Convex
   code changed) in this worktree, wait for "Ready", and exercise the changed path end to end: `curl`
   the route for the expected status and hit changed API routes. A passing typecheck/lint/build alone
   does not count.
2. **Verify visually with a screenshot.** Follow the visual-recreation steps above (headless Chrome,
   wide + narrow shot), then Read the PNG and look at it. For pages behind auth, use a temporary
   preview route with mock data. Non-UI changes still get a screenshot of the affected page to prove
   nothing regressed.
3. **Report** what was seen, what was not verified (hover/focus, auth-gated pages, animations), and
   the screenshot path. If the server can't boot (e.g. missing env vars), say so explicitly and fix
   the env first (see below); never claim success without having run it.
4. Clean up (stop the server, delete preview routes/temp files) before committing.

Env vars: each worktree needs its own copy of the gitignored `.env*` files. If `.env.local` is
missing in the current worktree, symlink it from the canonical copy at `~/.config/avian/.env.local`
(`ln -s ~/.config/avian/.env.local .env.local`) before starting the server.

"""neatlogs instrumentation. Every function no-ops if NEATLOGS_API_KEY is missing or neatlogs fails."""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import uuid
from typing import Any, Callable

WORKFLOW_NAME = "support-agent"
_enabled = False


def run_tags() -> list[str]:
    """Tags from env: AGENTBISECT_COMMIT, AGENTBISECT_RUN_ID, AGENTBISECT_CASE."""
    out = []
    for env, key in (("AGENTBISECT_COMMIT", "commit"), ("AGENTBISECT_RUN_ID", "run"), ("AGENTBISECT_CASE", "case")):
        if os.environ.get(env):
            out.append(f"{key}:{os.environ[env]}")
    return out


def init_tracing() -> bool:
    """Call once per process, before creating the model client. Tags are process-wide in neatlogs."""
    global _enabled
    if _enabled:
        return True
    if not os.environ.get("NEATLOGS_API_KEY"):
        return False
    try:
        import neatlogs

        neatlogs.init(api_key=os.environ["NEATLOGS_API_KEY"], workflow_name=WORKFLOW_NAME, tags=run_tags())
        _enabled = True
    except Exception:  # tracing must never break the agent
        _enabled = False
    return _enabled


def wrap_client(client: Any) -> Any:
    if not _enabled:
        return client
    import neatlogs

    return neatlogs.wrap(client)


def traced(fn: Callable) -> Callable:
    """Group a whole agent run into one root span (one trace) when tracing is on.

    Uses neatlogs' internal tracer because @neatlogs.span did not expose a recordable OTel span context
    (so the trace id could not be read). Falls back to untraced if that private API changes."""
    def inner(*a, **kw):
        if not _enabled:
            return fn(*a, **kw)
        try:
            from neatlogs._wrap_utils import get_tracer

            cm = get_tracer().start_as_current_span(
                "support-agent.run", attributes={"openinference.span.kind": "AGENT"})
        except Exception:
            return fn(*a, **kw)
        with cm:
            return fn(*a, **kw)
    inner.__name__ = fn.__name__
    return inner


def current_trace_id() -> str:
    """Hex OpenTelemetry trace id of the active span, or a local uuid when tracing is off."""
    try:
        from opentelemetry import trace

        ctx = trace.get_current_span().get_span_context()
        if ctx.is_valid:
            return format(ctx.trace_id, "032x")
    except Exception:
        pass
    return "local-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:16]


def shutdown_tracing() -> None:
    global _enabled
    if not _enabled:
        return
    try:
        import neatlogs

        neatlogs.flush()
        neatlogs.shutdown()
    except Exception:
        pass
    _enabled = False

import json
import re
import time
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from typing import Any

from agent.logs import log_message_truncated, log_tool_call
from agent.prompt import SYSTEM_PROMPT
from agent.provider import Provider
from agent.tracing import current_trace_id, traced
from tools import ToolBox

MAX_STEPS = 12  # model calls per run; leaves room for verification searches and retries
MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS = 2000  # longer customer messages are truncated (and the truncation logged)
_UNKNOWN_ORDER = re.compile(r"^order '(.*)' not found$")


def unknown_order_reply(order_id: str) -> str:
    return (f"Sorry, I couldn't find an order with the number {order_id}. Could you double-check the order "
            "number and send it again? Is there anything else we can help with?")


def _guard_unknown_order(reply: str, tool_calls: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> str:
    """Replace a reply that echoes a raw 'order ... not found' tool error with a customer-friendly apology."""
    for tc in tool_calls:
        err = tc["result"].get("error", "")
        m = _UNKNOWN_ORDER.match(err)
        if m and err.lower() in reply.lower():
            return unknown_order_reply(m.group(1))
    return reply


@dataclass
class RunResult:
    reply: str
    tool_calls: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)  # {name, args, result}
    steps: int = 0
    input_tokens: int = 0
    output_tokens: int = 0
    trace_id: str = ""
    hit_step_limit: bool = False

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return asdict(self)


def run_agent(message: str, provider: Provider, toolbox: ToolBox | None = None,
              max_steps: int | None = None) -> RunResult:
    """Run one customer message through the agent. `max_steps` defaults to MAX_STEPS.
    Messages longer than MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS are truncated to that length."""
    if len(message) > MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS:
        log_message_truncated(len(message), MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS)
        message = message[:MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS]
    return _run(message, provider, toolbox or ToolBox(), max_steps or MAX_STEPS)


@traced
def _run(message: str, provider: Provider, toolbox: ToolBox, max_steps: int) -> RunResult:
    res = RunResult(reply="", trace_id=current_trace_id())
    messages: list[dict[str, Any]] = [{"role": "user", "content": message}]
    for _ in range(max_steps):
        r = provider.create(system=SYSTEM_PROMPT, messages=messages, tools=toolbox.schemas)
        res.steps += 1
        res.input_tokens += r.input_tokens
        res.output_tokens += r.output_tokens
        if not r.tool_uses:
            res.reply = _guard_unknown_order(r.text, res.tool_calls)
            return res
        messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": r.content})
        results = []
        for tu in r.tool_uses:
            t0 = time.perf_counter()
            out = toolbox.call(tu["name"], tu["input"])
            log_tool_call(tu["name"], tu["input"], (time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000)
            res.tool_calls.append({"name": tu["name"], "args": tu["input"], "result": out})
            results.append({"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": tu["id"], "content": json.dumps(out)})
        messages.append({"role": "user", "content": results})
        res.reply = r.text
    res.hit_step_limit = True
    if not res.reply:
        res.reply = "Sorry, I could not finish handling this request. A human agent will follow up."
    return res
"""Run eval cases against the agent. Deterministic checks first, then budget, then the optional judge."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable

from evals import SCHEMA_VERSION, models
from evals.cases import Case
from evals.checks import run_checks

MAX_STEPS_BUDGET = 6
TOKEN_FACTOR = 1.5
BASELINE_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "baseline.json"
REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- baseline
class Baseline:
    """Per-case median tokens/steps from a good-commit run (written by `python -m evals calibrate`)."""

    def __init__(self, data: dict[str, Any], path: str | None = None) -> None:
        self.data, self.path = data, path
        self.cases: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = data.get("cases", {})

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path: Path | str | None = None) -> "Baseline | None":
        p = Path(path or BASELINE_PATH)
        return cls(json.loads(p.read_text()), str(p)) if p.exists() else None

    def token_limit(self, case_id: str) -> float | None:
        c = self.cases.get(case_id)
        return TOKEN_FACTOR * c["median_tokens"] if c else None


def build_baseline(results: list["CaseResult"], meta: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Medians over runs whose deterministic checks passed (budget ignored)."""
    by: dict[str, list[CaseResult]] = {}
    for r in results:
        if r.status in ("pass", "fail") and r.checks_passed:
            by.setdefault(r.case_id, []).append(r)
    return {
        "schema_version": SCHEMA_VERSION, "commit": meta.get("commit"), "created_at": _now(),
        "provider": meta.get("provider"),
        "agent_model": meta.get("agent_model"), "judge_model": meta.get("judge_model"), "token_factor": TOKEN_FACTOR, "max_steps": MAX_STEPS_BUDGET,
        "cases": {cid: {"median_tokens": statistics.median(r.tokens for r in rs),
                        "median_steps": statistics.median(r.steps for r in rs), "n": len(rs)}
                  for cid, rs in sorted(by.items())},
    }


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- results
@dataclass
class CaseResult:
    case_id: str
    category: str
    held_out: bool
    repeat: int = 0
    agent_model: str | None = None  # pinned ids, recorded in every result (see evals/models.py)
    judge_model: str | None = None
    status: str = "pass"  # pass | fail | skipped | error
    checks: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)
    checks_passed: bool | None = None
    budget: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    judge: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    reply: str = ""
    tool_calls: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)
    steps: int = 0
    input_tokens: int = 0
    output_tokens: int = 0
    tokens: int = 0
    trace_id: str = ""
    duration_s: float = 0.0
    reason: str | None = None  # skip / error explanation

    @property
    def passed(self) -> bool:
        return self.status == "pass"

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        d = asdict(self)
        d["passed"] = self.passed
        return d

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: dict[str, Any]) -> "CaseResult":
        d = {k: v for k, v in d.items() if k in cls.__dataclass_fields__}
        return cls(**d)


def _now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")


def budget_check(steps: int, tokens: int, case_id: str, baseline: Baseline | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """steps <= 6 always; tokens <= 1.5x baseline median when a baseline exists for the case."""
    b: dict[str, Any] = {"steps": steps, "max_steps": MAX_STEPS_BUDGET, "tokens": tokens,
                         "token_limit": None, "baseline_median_tokens": None}
    reasons = []
    if steps > MAX_STEPS_BUDGET:
        reasons.append(f"{steps} steps > {MAX_STEPS_BUDGET}")
    if baseline is None:
        b["token_check"] = "skipped: no baseline"
    elif (limit := baseline.token_limit(case_id)) is None:
        b["token_check"] = "skipped: case not in baseline"
    else:
        b["token_check"] = "checked"
        b["token_limit"], b["baseline_median_tokens"] = limit, baseline.cases[case_id]["median_tokens"]
        if tokens > limit:
            reasons.append(f"{tokens} tokens > limit {limit:.0f} ({TOKEN_FACTOR}x baseline median)")
    b["status"] = "fail" if reasons else ("pass" if b["token_check"] == "checked" else "partial")
    b["reason"] = "; ".join(reasons) or ("within budget" if b["status"] == "pass" else "steps ok; " + b["token_check"])
    return b


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- running
def run_case(case: Case, provider: Any, *, toolbox_factory: Callable[[], Any] | None = None,
             baseline: Baseline | None = None, judge: Any | None = None, repeat: int = 0,
             max_steps: int | None = None, agent_model: str | None = None,
             judge_model: str | None = None) -> CaseResult:
    """Run one case once. `provider` is a Provider. Never raises for agent/provider failures (status 'error').

    Tracing tags (commit/run/case) are process-wide, see evals/README.md; use run_suite(isolate=True) for
    per-case tags."""
    from agent.loop import run_agent
    from tools import ToolBox

    res = CaseResult(case.id, case.category, case.held_out, repeat=repeat,
                     agent_model=agent_model or getattr(provider, "model", None) or models.agent_model(),
                     judge_model=judge_model or getattr(judge, "model", None) or models.judge_model())
    toolbox = (toolbox_factory or ToolBox)()
    if case.requires_tool and case.requires_tool not in {s["name"] for s in toolbox.schemas}:
        res.status, res.reason = "skipped", f"requires tool '{case.requires_tool}' which this commit does not have"
        return res
    t0 = time.time()
    try:
        run = run_agent(case.input, provider, toolbox, max_steps)
    except Exception as e:  # provider/network/agent crash: infra problem, not a behavioral verdict
        res.status, res.reason, res.duration_s = "error", f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}", round(time.time() - t0, 3)
        return res
    res.duration_s = round(time.time() - t0, 3)
    res.reply, res.tool_calls, res.steps, res.trace_id = run.reply, run.tool_calls, run.steps, run.trace_id
    res.input_tokens, res.output_tokens = run.input_tokens, run.output_tokens
    res.tokens = run.input_tokens + run.output_tokens
    res.checks = run_checks(case.checks, run)
    res.checks_passed = all(c["passed"] for c in res.checks)
    res.budget = budget_check(res.steps, res.tokens, case.id, baseline)
    ok = res.checks_passed and res.budget["status"] != "fail"
    if judge is not None and case.rubric and res.checks_passed:  # judge only after deterministic checks pass
        try:
            res.judge = judge.judge(case, run)
        except Exception as e:
            res.judge = {"passed": False, "reason": f"judge error: {e}"}
        ok = ok and res.judge["passed"]
    res.status = "pass" if ok else "fail"
    return res


def _make_provider(provider: Any, case: Case) -> Any:
    """`provider` is a Provider, or a callable(case) -> Provider (needed for ScriptedProvider, which is consumed)."""
    return provider if hasattr(provider, "create") else provider(case)


def run_suite(cases: list[Case], provider: Any, *, repeats: int = 1, isolate: bool = False,
              toolbox_factory: Callable[[], Any] | None = None, baseline: Baseline | None = None,
              judge: Any | None = None, meta: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
              child_args: list[str] | None = None, progress: Callable[[CaseResult], None] | None = None
              ) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Run every case `repeats` times and return the report dict (see evals/README.md)."""
    meta = {**models.pinned(), **{k: v for k, v in (meta or {}).items() if v is not None}}
    if baseline is not None:  # never judge a run against a baseline made under different pinned models
        models.assert_comparable(baseline.data, meta)
    results: list[CaseResult] = []
    for case in cases:
        for rep in range(repeats):
            if isolate:
                r = run_case_isolated(case, rep, child_args or [], meta or {})
            else:
                r = run_case(case, _make_provider(provider, case), toolbox_factory=toolbox_factory,
                             baseline=baseline, judge=judge, repeat=rep,
                             agent_model=meta["agent_model"], judge_model=meta["judge_model"])
            results.append(r)
            if progress:
                progress(r)
    return build_report(results, cases, repeats=repeats, baseline=baseline, isolated=isolate, meta=meta)


def run_case_isolated(case: Case, repeat: int, child_args: list[str], meta: dict[str, Any]) -> CaseResult:
    """Run one case in a fresh `python -m evals` subprocess so neatlogs tags (process-wide) are per case."""
    env = {**os.environ, "AGENTBISECT_CASE": case.id}
    for key, name in (("commit", "AGENTBISECT_COMMIT"), ("run_id", "AGENTBISECT_RUN_ID")):
        if meta.get(key):
            env[name] = str(meta[key])
    cmd = [sys.executable, "-m", "evals", "run", "--suite", "all", "--cases", case.id, "--repeats", "1",
           "--json", *child_args]
    try:
        p = subprocess.run(cmd, env=env, cwd=REPO_ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=600)
        out = json.loads(p.stdout)
        r = CaseResult.from_dict(out["results"][0])
    except Exception as e:
        stderr = locals().get("p") and p.stderr[-300:]
        r = CaseResult(case.id, case.category, case.held_out, status="error",
                       agent_model=meta.get("agent_model"), judge_model=meta.get("judge_model"),
                       reason=f"isolated run failed: {type(e).__name__}: {e} {stderr or ''}".strip())
    r.repeat = repeat
    return r


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- report
def _rate(num: int, den: int) -> float | None:
    return round(num / den, 4) if den else None


def build_report(results: list[CaseResult], cases: list[Case], *, repeats: int, baseline: Baseline | None,
                 isolated: bool, meta: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    ran = [r for r in results if r.status in ("pass", "fail")]
    bud = [r for r in ran if r.budget.get("status") in ("pass", "fail")]
    per_case = []
    for c in cases:
        rs = [r for r in results if r.case_id == c.id]
        ex = [r for r in rs if r.status in ("pass", "fail")]
        eb = [r for r in ex if r.budget.get("status") in ("pass", "fail")]
        n_pass = sum(r.passed for r in rs)
        if rs and all(r.status == "skipped" for r in rs):
            st = "skipped"
        elif rs and all(r.status == "error" for r in rs):
            st = "error"
        elif ex and n_pass == len(ex):
            st = "pass"
        elif n_pass == 0:
            st = "fail"
        else:
            st = "flaky"
        per_case.append({
            "case_id": c.id, "category": c.category, "held_out": c.held_out, "status": st,
            "runs": len(rs), "passed": n_pass, "failed": sum(r.status == "fail" for r in rs),
            "skipped": sum(r.status == "skipped" for r in rs), "errors": sum(r.status == "error" for r in rs),
            "pass_rate": _rate(n_pass, len(ex)),
            "checks_pass_rate": _rate(sum(bool(r.checks_passed) for r in ex), len(ex)),
            "budget_pass_rate": _rate(sum(r.budget["status"] == "pass" for r in eb), len(eb)),
            "mean_tokens": round(statistics.mean(r.tokens for r in ex), 1) if ex else None,
            "mean_steps": round(statistics.mean(r.steps for r in ex), 2) if ex else None,
        })
    n_pass = sum(r.passed for r in results)
    return {
        "schema_version": SCHEMA_VERSION,
        "commit": meta.get("commit"), "run_id": meta.get("run_id"), "suite": meta.get("suite"),
        "provider": meta.get("provider"),
        "agent_model": meta.get("agent_model"), "judge_model": meta.get("judge_model"), "repeats": repeats, "isolated": isolated,
        "started_at": meta.get("started_at") or _now(), "finished_at": _now(),
        "baseline": {"loaded": baseline is not None, "path": baseline.path if baseline else None,
                     "commit": baseline.data.get("commit") if baseline else None,
                     "budget_check": ("active" if baseline else "token budget skipped: no baseline (steps still checked)")},
        "summary": {
            "total_runs": len(results), "executed": len(ran), "passed": n_pass,
            "failed": sum(r.status == "fail" for r in results), "skipped": sum(r.status == "skipped" for r in results),
            "errors": sum(r.status == "error" for r in results),
            "pass_rate": _rate(n_pass, len(ran)),
            "checks_pass_rate": _rate(sum(bool(r.checks_passed) for r in ran), len(ran)),
            "budget_pass_rate": _rate(sum(r.budget["status"] == "pass" for r in bud), len(bud)),
            "total_tokens": sum(r.tokens for r in ran),
        },
        "cases": per_case,
        "results": [r.to_dict() for r in results],
    }


def compare_reports(a: dict[str, Any], b: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Per-case status/pass-rate diff between two reports. Raises ModelConfigError if the reports were produced
    under different pinned agent/judge models (or either lacks them): the comparison would be meaningless."""
    models.assert_comparable(a, b)
    ca, cb = {c["case_id"]: c for c in a["cases"]}, {c["case_id"]: c for c in b["cases"]}
    return {cid: {"from": ca[cid]["status"], "to": cb[cid]["status"], "pass_rate": [ca[cid]["pass_rate"], cb[cid]["pass_rate"]]}
            for cid in ca.keys() & cb.keys() if ca[cid]["status"] != cb[cid]["status"]}

## boardui
BoardUI is a React + Tailwind CSS v4 design system (Next.js first) with free components and paid Pro components/templates. This server installs component source directly into the user's project — no terminal needed.

Typical flow:
1. In a project without BoardUI, call init_boardui once (installs Tailwind v4 + runtime deps, writes styles/ and utils/).
2. Discover with list_components; read source/props with get_component; get working code with get_usage_examples.
3. Install with install_components — it writes the files and installs npm deps.

Component names are exact — when unsure, call list_components instead of guessing.

"""Model provider layer.

A Provider turns (system, messages, tools) into a normalized Response. Select with env AGENT_PROVIDER
("anthropic" is the default; "scripted" is for tests and is constructed directly).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Protocol

DEFAULT_MODEL = "claude-haiku-5-5"  # the support agent is PINNED to Haiku tier; see evals/models.py


@dataclass
class Response:
    """Normalized model response. `content` is a list of Anthropic-style blocks:
    {"type": "text", "text": ...} or {"type": "tool_use", "id": ..., "name": ..., "input": {...}}."""

    content: list[dict[str, Any]]
    stop_reason: str = "end_turn"
    input_tokens: int = 0
    output_tokens: int = 0

    @property
    def text(self) -> str:
        return "".join(b["text"] for b in self.content if b["type"] == "text")

    @property
    def tool_uses(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        return [b for b in self.content if b["type"] == "tool_use"]


class Provider(Protocol):
    def create(self, *, system: str, messages: list[dict[str, Any]], tools: list[dict[str, Any]],
               max_tokens: int = 1024) -> Response: ...


class AnthropicProvider:
    """Anthropic Messages API. Key from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, model from AGENT_MODEL, temperature 0."""

    def __init__(self, client: Any | None = None, model: str | None = None) -> None:
        if client is None:
            from anthropic import Anthropic

            from agent.tracing import wrap_client

            client = wrap_client(Anthropic())  # reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
        self.client = client
        self.model = model or os.environ.get("AGENT_MODEL", DEFAULT_MODEL)

    def create(self, *, system, messages, tools, max_tokens=1024) -> Response:
        r = self.client.messages.create(
            model=self.model, max_tokens=max_tokens,
            extra_body={"temperature": 0},  # SDK 1.x dropped the typed kwarg; the API still accepts it
            system=system, messages=messages, tools=tools,
        )
        blocks: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        for b in r.content:
            if b.type == "text":
                blocks.append({"type": "text", "text": b.text})
            elif b.type == "tool_use":
                blocks.append({"type": "tool_use", "id": b.id, "name": b.name, "input": dict(b.input)})
        return Response(blocks, r.stop_reason or "end_turn", r.usage.input_tokens, r.usage.output_tokens)


@dataclass
class ScriptedProvider:
    """Replays a fixed list of Responses (for tests). Records every call in `calls`."""

    script: list[Response]
    calls: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)

    def create(self, *, system, messages, tools, max_tokens=1024) -> Response:
        self.calls.append({"system": system, "messages": [dict(m) for m in messages], "tools": tools})
        if not self.script:
            raise RuntimeError("ScriptedProvider script exhausted")
        return self.script.pop(0)


# EXTENSION POINT: add other backends (AWS Bedrock, `claude` CLI, ...) as classes implementing
# Provider.create and register them in _FACTORIES. Not implemented on purpose.
_FACTORIES = {"anthropic": AnthropicProvider}


def get_provider(name: str | None = None) -> Provider:
    name = (name or os.environ.get("AGENT_PROVIDER", "anthropic")).lower()
    if name not in _FACTORIES:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown AGENT_PROVIDER '{name}'; available: {sorted(_FACTORIES)}")
    return _FACTORIES[name]()

from tools.impl import PINNED_TODAY, ToolBox, TOOL_SCHEMAS

__all__ = ["PINNED_TODAY", "ToolBox", "TOOL_SCHEMAS"]

"""Pinned model identities for the eval pipeline.

Roles: the support agent (cheap, Haiku tier) is the lab rat; the judge must be a strictly smarter model.
Both ids are recorded in every eval result so a model never silently drifts between commits, and results
produced under different pinned models refuse to be compared.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
from typing import Any

DEFAULT_AGENT_MODEL = "claude-haiku-5-5"
DEFAULT_JUDGE_MODEL = "claude-sonnet-5-5"

TIERS = {"haiku": 1, "sonnet": 2, "opus": 3, "fable": 3}  # haiku < sonnet < opus/fable


class ModelConfigError(ValueError):
    """Raised when pinned models are misconfigured or results from different pins are mixed."""


def tier(model: str) -> int:
    """Tier rank of a model id by substring ('claude-haiku-5-5' -> 1). Unknown families raise."""
    m = model.lower()
    for name, rank in TIERS.items():
        if name in m:
            return rank
    raise ModelConfigError(f"cannot determine tier of model '{model}' (expected haiku/sonnet/opus/fable in id)")


def agent_model() -> str:
    return os.environ.get("AGENT_MODEL") or DEFAULT_AGENT_MODEL


def judge_model() -> str:
    return os.environ.get("JUDGE_MODEL") or DEFAULT_JUDGE_MODEL


def check_judge_model(judge: str, agent: str) -> None:
    """Fail loudly unless the judge is a different model, not haiku-tier, and a higher tier than the agent."""
    if judge == agent:
        raise ModelConfigError(f"judge model must differ from agent model (both are '{judge}')")
    jt, at = tier(judge), tier(agent)
    if jt <= TIERS["haiku"]:

def _normalize_email(email: str) -> str:
    """Case-insensitive, whitespace-free key; emails never legitimately contain whitespace."""
    return "".join(email.split()).casefold()


_ORDER_ID_PREFIX = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:order\b)?[\s#]*", re.IGNORECASE)


def _normalize_order_id(order_id: str) -> str:
    """Drop how customers write ids ('#1042', 'order 1042', ' 1042 '); leading zeros are significant."""
    return _ORDER_ID_PREFIX.sub("", str(order_id)).strip()


def _with_delivery_estimate(o: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Copy of the order plus estimated_delivery_date (ship date + 5 days) when shipped, else None."""
    eta = None
    if o["status"] == "shipped" and o["ship_date"]:
        eta = (date.fromisoformat(o["ship_date"]) + timedelta(days=DELIVERY_ESTIMATE_DAYS)).isoformat()
    return {**o, "estimated_delivery_date": eta}


class ToolBox:
    """Per-run tool state (refunds issued, tickets opened). Create a fresh one for every run."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.orders: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {
            o["order_id"]: o for o in json.loads((DATA_DIR / "orders.json").read_text())
        }
        self.articles: list[dict[str, Any]] = json.loads((DATA_DIR / "articles.json").read_text())
        self._refund_seq = 100  # seed data uses RF-0001
        self._ticket_seq = 0

    @property
    def schemas(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        return copy.deepcopy(TOOL_SCHEMAS)

    def call(self, name: str, args: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        fn = getattr(self, f"_tool_{name}", None) if name in {s["name"] for s in self.schemas} else None
        if fn is None:
            return {"error": f"unknown tool '{name}'"}
        try:
            return fn(**args)
        except TypeError as e:
            return {"error": f"bad arguments: {e}"}

    # -- tools ---------------------------------------------------------
    def _tool_lookup_order(self, order_id: str | None = None, email: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
        oid = _normalize_order_id(order_id) if order_id else ""
        if oid:
            o = self.orders.get(oid)
            return {"orders": [_with_delivery_estimate(o)]} if o else {"error": f"order '{oid}' not found"}
        key = _normalize_email(email) if email else ""
        if key:
            found = [o for o in self.orders.values() if _normalize_email(o["customer_email"]) == key]
            return {"orders": [_with_delivery_estimate(o) for o in found]} if found else {"error": f"no orders for '{email.strip()}'"}
        return {"error": "provide order_id or email"}

    def _tool_search_help(self, query: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        q = query.lower()
        words = {w for w in q.replace("?", " ").split() if len(w) > 2}

        def score(a: dict[str, Any]) -> int:
            s = sum(3 for k in a["keywords"] if k in q)
            s += sum(1 for w in words if w in a["body"].lower() or w in a["title"].lower())
            return s

        # Explicit tie-break, independent of articles.json order: core policy articles first, then by id.
        def tie_break(a: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[int, str]:
            return (CORE_ARTICLE_PRIORITY.index(a["id"]) if a["id"] in CORE_ARTICLE_PRIORITY
                    else len(CORE_ARTICLE_PRIORITY), a["id"])

        ranked = sorted(self.articles, key=lambda a: (-score(a), *tie_break(a)))[:3]
        return {"articles": [{"id": a["id"], "title": a["title"], "body": a["body"]} for a in ranked]}

    def _tool_issue_refund(self, order_id: str, amount: int, reason: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        o = self.orders.get(str(order_id))
        if not o:
            return {"error": f"order '{order_id}' not found"}
        if o["refund_id"]:
            return {"error": f"order {order_id} was already refunded ({o['refund_id']})"}
        if o["status"] != "delivered" or not o["delivered_date"]:
            return {"error": f"order {order_id} is {o['status']}, not delivered; cannot refund"}
        days = (PINNED_TODAY - date.fromisoformat(o["delivered_date"])).days
        if days > REFUND_WINDOW_DAYS:
            return {"error": f"order {order_id} was delivered {days} days ago; refund window is {REFUND_WINDOW_DAYS} days"}
        # Integer cents only, like Stripe: a float (e.g. 64.0) is most likely dollars passed by mistake.
        if isinstance(amount, bool) or not isinstance(amount, int) or amount <= 0:
            return {"error": "amount must be a positive integer number of US cents (e.g. 6400 for $64.00)"}
        total_cents = round(o["total_usd"] * 100)
        if amount > total_cents:
            return {"error": f"amount {amount} cents (${amount / 100:.2f}) exceeds order total "
                             f"{total_cents} cents (${total_cents / 100:.2f})"}
        self._refund_seq += 1
        rid = f"RF-{self._refund_seq:04d}"
        o["refund_id"] = rid
        return {"refund_id": rid, "order_id": order_id, "amount": amount, "currency": "usd", "reason": reason}

    def _tool_cancel_order(self, order_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        oid = _normalize_order_id(order_id)
        o = self.orders.get(oid)
        if not o:
            return {"error": f"order '{oid}' not found"}
        if o["status"] != "processing":
            return {"error": f"order {oid} is {o['status']}; only unshipped (processing) orders can be cancelled"}
        o["status"] = "cancelled"
        return {"confirmation": f"CXL-{oid}", "order_id": oid, "status": "cancelled"}

    def _tool_escalate_to_human(self, summary: str, priority: str, order_id: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
        if priority not in {"low", "normal", "high", "urgent"}:
            return {"error": "priority must be one of low, normal, high, urgent"}
        # Make sure the ticket names the order; digit lookarounds so '1088' is not found inside '10880'.
        oid = _normalize_order_id(order_id) if order_id else ""
        if oid and not re.search(rf"(?<!\d){re.escape(oid)}(?!\d)", summary):
            summary = f"Order {oid}: {summary}"
        self._ticket_seq += 1
        return {"ticket_id": f"TKT-{self._ticket_seq:04d}", "priority": priority, "summary": summary}

def format_tool_calls(tool_calls: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> str:
